title: You've Been Replaced, First Love
platform_source: TWO independent sources agree. (1) The FILENAME begins 'Reelshort - ', which adapters.md sec 23 makes authoritative. (2) The PDF's own Details block, page 7: 'Production companies  Swzz Media Productions  ReelShort'. First title in this batch where both could be checked against each other.
IMPORT_CANDIDATE: NOT in titles.csv. One of Armand Procacci's 33 missing titles. Now has platform, year, release date, aka and 18 cast - everything to create it properly except poster and synopsis, which only the platform supplies.
METHOD_THIS_PROVES: A LOCAL PDF CAN BE PAIRED AS RELIABLY AS A DRIVE FILE. Two steps, both needed. (1) pypdf exposes the page's LINK ANNOTATIONS, and IMDb's cast links carry ?ref_=tt_cst_t_N, giving the billing ORDER and the nm id for each slot. (2) pypdf's extract_text(extraction_mode='layout') preserves the two-column grid, so each row reads 'left actor | right actor' then 'left character | right character'. INDENTATION IS THE LOAD-BEARING SIGNAL - stripping whitespace destroys the only thing that says which column a lone character belongs to.
HOW_THE_AMBIGUITY_WAS_SETTLED: Flat text gave 'Armand Procacci Jason CaceresAlexAshley DavidsonJessieClaire KerofskyKate', which reads equally well as 'Procacci -> Jason Caceres' or 'Procacci -> Jason, Caceres -> Alex'. Layout mode shows 'Alex' at indent 92, the RIGHT column, so it belongs to Jason Caceres, who is an ACTOR not a character. Cyan read it that way unaided. Slot 3's nm is nm11768336 - Procacci's own id in people.csv - which independently confirms the whole slot ordering.
pairing_method: Ordered nm ids from PDF link annotations (tt_cst_t_1..18), aligned to a two-column layout grid read left-to-right, top-to-bottom. Confirmed by slot 3 = nm11768336 = Armand Procacci.
cast_count_note: IMDb says Top Cast 24. Eighteen carry nm links in the saved pages; the remaining six are not present in this PDF and are NOT invented.
